title: HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core: A Gaming Headset for Long Ranked Sessions
summary: The HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core (683L9AA) is HyperX's budget wired gaming headset: 40 mm drivers, about 272 g, a swivel-to-mute mic, on-ear volume control and a 2-year warranty. At around 750K VND, is it worth it for new gamers?
description:
## Who is it for?

- New PC or console gamers who need a headset with a good mic under 800K VND.
- Students who study online and game.
- People who want a light headset for long sessions.
- People who want a gaming brand with a 2-year warranty.

## Why buy it?

- Light at about 272 g with soft ear cushions.
- Swivel-to-mute mic.
- Volume control on the ear cup.
- 3.5 mm jack works with PC, consoles and phones.
- 2-year warranty.

specs.label: Drivers
specs.value: 40 mm dynamic with neodymium magnets, directional, enhanced bass

specs.label: Microphone
specs.value: Electret condenser, noise-cancelling, swivel-to-mute, flexible boom

specs.label: Controls
specs.value: Volume control on the ear cup

specs.label: Connection
specs.value: 3.5 mm (4-pole) jack, plus a PC splitter cable with dual 3.5 mm

specs.label: Compatibility
specs.value: PC; works with PS5/PS4, Xbox, Switch and phones via 3.5 mm

specs.label: Ear cushions
specs.value: Soft foam with fabric, plastic frame, slider adjustment

specs.label: Warranty
specs.value: 2 years (HyperX); 24 months via distributors in Vietnam depending on the seller

sections.title: What is the HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core?
sections.content: HyperX is a well-known gaming gear brand (owned by HP), and the Cloud Stinger 2 Core (model 683L9AA) is the cheapest wired gaming headset in the second-generation Cloud Stinger line. HyperX calls it an entry-level headset focused on the basics: good sound, comfort and convenience. In Vietnam it's sold officially for about 745–750K VND (CellphoneS, Phong Vu, ThinkPro) with a 24-month warranty; on HyperX's official store it's about US$29.99.

sections.title: Design: light and comfortable for long sessions
sections.content: The headset weighs about 272 g — light for an over-ear gaming headset, so it won't weigh on your head during long sessions. The closed-back over-ear design helps you focus on the game and limits sound leakage. The ear cushions use soft foam wrapped in fabric, which feels less stuffy and hot than leatherette in Vietnam's climate, at the cost of slightly weaker passive isolation. The frame is plastic, with sliders on both sides for size adjustment. The design is simple and black, with no RGB.

sections.title: Sound: 40 mm drivers with enhanced bass
sections.content: The Cloud Stinger 2 Core uses 40 mm dynamic drivers with neodymium magnets in a directional design that aims sound straight into your ears, tuned by HyperX for enhanced bass. Frequency response is 10Hz–25kHz, sensitivity 95 dB and THD under 2%. At this price, reasonable expectations are punchy explosions and gunfire, footsteps clear enough for mainstream shooters, and decent music and movies. There's no hardware 7.1 surround; some Vietnamese sellers include a DTS Headphone:X activation code (software spatial audio on PC) for 2 years — if you need it, ask the seller before buying.

sections.title: Swivel-to-mute microphone
sections.content: The mic is a noise-cancelling electret condenser on a flexible boom, so you can position it close to your mouth. The handiest feature is swivel-to-mute: flip the mic up and it's definitely muted, no need to check software or an indicator light. For Discord, team games or online meetings, mic quality at this price is clear enough. Note that the mic is fixed and can't be removed, so the headset isn't great as an on-the-go music headphone.

sections.title: Connectivity and compatibility
sections.content: The headset uses a 4-pole 3.5 mm jack and comes with a splitter to dual 3.5 mm (headphone and mic) for PCs with separate audio ports. Thanks to the 3.5 mm jack, you can plug it into PS5/PS4 and Xbox controllers, the Nintendo Switch, laptops or phones that still have a 3.5 mm port (USB-C-only phones need an adapter). The volume control sits on the ear cup. As a wired analog headset, it needs no drivers or software — plug and play, with no battery or latency worries.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't?
sections.content: Buy it if you're a new PC or console gamer who needs a headset with a good mic under 800K VND; a student who studies online and games; or want a light, comfortable headset from a gaming brand with a 2-year warranty. Skip it if you need wireless, 7.1 surround or RGB, want a sturdier metal frame (the pricier HyperX Cloud II or Cloud III), or need a headset you can also wear outdoors (the mic isn't removable).

sections.title: Where this review's information comes from
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used this product hands-on. This review compiles and analyzes HyperX's official product page and specifications (hyperx.com), along with prices and warranty terms from Vietnamese retailers (CellphoneS, Phong Vu, ThinkPro), as of October 2026. Images in this article are HyperX's official product images. Comments on sound are based on specifications and product positioning, not our own measurements. Prices may change over time — check the product page before ordering.

sections.title: Should you buy the HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core?
sections.content: The HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core is a dependable entry-level gaming headset under 800K VND: light, comfortable, a swivel-to-mute mic, on-ear volume control, a 3.5 mm jack that works with many devices and a 2-year warranty from a major gaming brand. It lacks wireless, RGB and hardware surround, and the plastic frame isn't as durable as higher models. If you need your first wired gaming headset that does the basics well, it's a safe choice.

pros: Light at about 272 g with soft cushions, comfortable for hours of gaming.
Swivel-to-mute mic — quick and certain, no software needed.
Volume control right on the ear cup, handy mid-game.
40 mm directional drivers with enhanced bass, good enough for games and everyday music.
3.5 mm jack works with PC, consoles and phones; PC splitter included.
HyperX brand, 2-year warranty and official distribution in Vietnam.
cons: Wired only, no wireless or USB.
The mic is fixed and can't be removed for on-the-go listening.
All-plastic frame, less durable than metal-frame models like the Cloud II.
No hardware 7.1 surround; whether a DTS Headphone:X code is included depends on the seller.
Fabric cushions stay cooler than leatherette but isolate less.
buying_advice: Worth buying for new gamers and students who need a headset with a good mic; if you need wireless or RGB, choose a higher model.

faq.question: Does the HyperX Cloud Stinger 2 Core work with PS5, Xbox and phones?
faq.answer: Yes. With a 3.5 mm jack it plugs into PS5/PS4 and Xbox controllers, the Nintendo Switch and phones with a 3.5 mm port. USB-C-only phones need a USB-C to 3.5 mm adapter.

faq.question: Does it have 7.1 surround sound?
faq.answer: There's no hardware 7.1 surround. Some sellers include a DTS Headphone:X activation code (software spatial audio on PC); if you need it, ask the seller before buying.

faq.question: Is the microphone detachable?
faq.answer: No. The mic is attached to the ear cup, but you can swivel it up to mute and bend the boom to adjust its position.

faq.question: How heavy is it, and is it comfortable for long sessions?
faq.answer: About 272 g, fairly light for an over-ear headset. Soft fabric-wrapped foam cushions keep it comfortable for hours and cooler than leatherette.

faq.question: How is the Cloud Stinger 2 Core different from the Cloud Stinger 2?
faq.answer: The Core is a trimmed-down, cheaper version focused on the basics. The Cloud Stinger 2 usually adds extras such as improved cushions and DTS support; if your budget allows, compare them before buying.

faq.question: How long is the warranty?
faq.answer: HyperX offers a 2-year warranty; authorized Vietnamese retailers such as ThinkPro list 24 months via the brand or distributor.
